results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. The calyx is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents. The pedunculus is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes. The mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: There are multiple types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain. These include [KCab-c(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, dorsal, and claw-count classes. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.title: Gene expression
results.question: What neurotransmitter do mushroom body Kenyon cells use?
results.response: Mushroom body Kenyon cells, such as alpha/beta core Kenyon cells, use acetylcholine as their primary neurotransmitter. VFB does not currently hold data on other neurotransmitters that alpha/beta core Kenyon cells may use.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to several brain regions. VFB records show neurons with presynaptic terminals in antennal lobe and neurons with postsynaptic terminals in antennal lobe, indicating connections to and from the antennal lobe. VFB has annotated tracts/nerves innervating antennal lobe, suggesting connections to other brain regions. However, VFB does not currently hold data on the specific brain regions that the antennal lobe connects to.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
Approximately more than 125,000 neurons.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- more than 125,000 neurons (adult Drosophila central brain connectome/model) — A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. — PMID 39358519
- ~139,255 neurons (whole adult Drosophila brain) — Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. — PMID 39358518

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions including navigation/orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal or memory-related behaviours.

results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response: Dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons comes from specific types of dopaminergic neurons, including dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and dopaminergic PAM neurons. The connectome data indicates that dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and adult dopaminergic PAM neurons are among the upstream class-connectivity partners of mushroom body output neurons. VFB records show that there are 84 upstream class-connectivity partners matching "dopaminergic neuron" for mushroom body output neurons, with top mapped pairs including dopaminergic PPL1 neuron and [adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049839 "Open adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). The specific connections between different types of dopaminergic neurons and mushroom body output neurons are not fully detailed in the available information, but it is clear that dopaminergic PPL1 and PAM neurons provide dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind, with distinct dendritic arbors in each lobula plate layer. It detects looming stimuli and projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP. The activity of this neuron elicits a jump escape response. VFB does not currently hold data on other connections of the lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2.

results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") compares between adult and larval Drosophila in terms of glomerular organization, with the adult having approximately 50 glomeruli and the larval having around 22 glomeruli. results.title: Publications for a circuit
results.question: What publications describe the PPL1 dopaminergic neurons and their role in aversive memory?
results.response: Publications describing the dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and their role in aversive memory include Claridge-Chang et al., 2009, Mao and Davis, 2009, Budnik and White, 1988, and Ren et al., 2016. These studies are associated with the formation of labile aversive memory, a dopamine-modulated neural circuit regulating aversive taste memory in Drosophila, and three dopamine pathways that induce aversive odor memories with different stability.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. It has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. This neuron is a [primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047097 "Open primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). 

The giant fiber neuron can be identified by its large descending axon, which crosses the midline and has an axonal lateral bend. 

VFB holds records of several neuron types, including [adult VNC neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00059289 "Open adult VNC neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [thoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001983 "Open thoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047096 "Open secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch OFF hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049540 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [mesothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001985 "Open mesothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), primary neuron, [Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049542 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [prothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001984 "Open prothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049539 "Open Notch ON hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB2-4 lineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048927 "Open NB2-4 lineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049541 "Open Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), but it does not currently hold data on the specific driver lines available for the giant fiber neuron. 

Publications by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), Power (1948), King and Wyman (1980), Allen et al. (1998), Kennedy and Broadie (2018), Dorkenwald et al. (2024), and Schlegel et al. (2024) provide relevant information on the giant fiber neuron.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response: Neuron types that might mediate a connection between the visual system and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") include projection neurons and visual projection neurons. Adult visual projection neurons to the mushroom body have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. This suggests that visual information could reach the memory circuit via these neuron types. VFB does not currently hold data on other neuron types that might be involved in this connection.

results.title: Novel circuit exploration
results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
results.response: The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") suggests that temperature information could influence memory formation. Thermosensory projection neurons relay temperature-detecting neurons to higher brain centers and VFB evidence supports a plausible thermosensory influence on mushroom-body memory circuitry through thermosensory projection neurons. VFB holds records of various neuron types, including [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [projection neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007392 "Open projection neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [local neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051493 "Open local neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), which may be relevant to understanding the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body.

results.title: API: VFB-connect (Python)
results.question: How do I install and get started with VFB-connect in Python?
results.response:
To install and get started with VFB-connect in Python, you can install it via PyPi. The installation command is:
```
pip install vfb-connect
```
This will install VFB-connect, allowing you to use it in your Python environment.

results.title: API: REST endpoints
results.question: How can I query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically using the SOLR or Owlery API?
results.response: To query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically, you can use the SOLR or Owlery API. The Owlery API provides OWL reasoning services for Virtual Fly Brain's ontologies, enabling complex queries over class hierarchies and relationships. You can access the Owlery API at https://owl.virtualflybrain.org/ and use various operations such as knowledgebase operations, DL queries, and SPARQL services. The SOLR Search API provides fast text search and autocomplete functionality for Virtual Fly Brain entities, datasets, and publications.

results.title: Workshops / training
results.question: What materials are available from the VFB 'Hacking the connectome' workshop?
results.response:
Materials from the VFB 'Hacking the connectome' workshop are available. The workshop materials include a recorded introduction session and workshop notebooks that demonstrate how to use available tools to explore and analyze published connectomes on VFB. 

```
https://www.virtualflybrain.org/docs/past-workshops/connectome
```

results.title: Anatomy teaching diagrams
results.question: Is there a circuit diagram of the mushroom body available on Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response: There is a schematic representation of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") available. VFB records show neurons with some part in mushroom body, neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body, and parts of mushroom body. The compartmental organisation of the [adult mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003684 "Open adult mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") lobes is described, including how the dendrites of mushroom body output neurons and the axon terminals of dopaminergic neurons tile the lobes into a stereotyped grid of 15 compartments.
